title: [Chapitre] IX et IX bis. [Ateliers] : notes manuscrites (05-15/07/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: Chapter IX of Grothendieck's 1986 notes on 'ateliers', an axiomatic order-theoretic notion of a 'workshop' of figures, ordered by inclusion and an extended relation ⊴. The previous page constructs, for any atelier A, a base structure Σ = Σ_A and a canonical morphism A → Atspat(Σ), X ↦ Disp(X). This morphism is faithful: X ⊂ Y iff Disp X ⊂ Disp Y. When A is already of the form Atspat(Σ), the map is a bijection. 'A is spatial' is to mean that this morphism is injective, so it identifies A with a sub-atelier of Atspat(Σ).

This page draws the consequence. A spatial atelier is equivalent to two data: (1) a base structure Σ, carrying an order ≤ and a covering-type datum C (Grothendieck's word for this structure is hard to read); (2) a subset A ⊂ Atspat(Σ). A sub-atelier here simply means a subset satisfying an earlier closure condition (cf. p. 27); in fact it is a subset closed under ⊴.

The analogy is with set-theoretic ateliers based on a set L, the 'cas ensembliste' of ch. VIII:
- Ateliers 1: closure under sub-figures.
- Ateliers 2: ∀x∈L, {{x}} ∈ A, i.e. every point occurs as a minimal figure.
A replacement for Ateliers 2 is needed in the Σ-relative setting. The next page supplies it as Atspat 2': with Σ' = {X^0 | X ∈ A}, every S ∈ Σ is the Sup of the elements of Σ' lying below it. This is a density / generating-basis condition, as for a basis of a locale or a join-dense subset of a lattice.

Grothendieck then conjectures a reconstruction statement. Data (≤, C, A) satisfying the axioms yield a spatial atelier, and the canonical map gives Σ ≃ Σ_A. Spatial ateliers would thus be classified by pairs (base Σ, ⊴-closed, join-dense family of figures). The pattern is the familiar one of spatial locales versus spaces, or of a site recovered from a dense family of generators.
errors: No mathematical error on this page. The page only sets up a classification; the equivalence is merely expected ('Je m'attends que', next page) and not proved here.
The words 'les deux seules (?) conditions' on the next page show Grothendieck himself was unsure whether the two axioms suffice.

ideas.what: Spatial atelier described as a base structure Σ plus a ⊴-closed family of figures A ⊂ Atspat(Σ)
ideas.modern_name: Representation / reconstruction theorem (like spatial locales ↔ sober spaces, or a lattice recovered from a join-dense subset)
ideas.usually_credited_to: General pattern: Stone duality, the Ehresmann/Bénabou/Isbell locale theory
ideas.where_published: Ateliers notes (cote 156-9) unpublished as far as known

ideas.what: Replacing the 'singletons are figures' axiom (Ateliers 2) by a density axiom: every S is the Sup of figure-supports below it

missed.claim: The conjectured equivalence between spatial ateliers and data (Σ, ≤, C, A) with axioms 1' and 2' is formulated as an expectation, not proved, on this and the next page. The whole 'atelier' theory appears absent from the literature.
missed.quote: Il faut une condition qui tienne lieu de Ateliers 2 (∀x∈L, {{x}}∈A)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is a minor, likely routine reconstruction result. It is of interest mainly for documenting Grothendieck's late, unpublished axiomatics of 'ateliers', not as a new mathematical result.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a standard representation-style setup (base structure plus a closed, dense family of figures). Its interest is mostly historical: it belongs to the unpublished 'ateliers' axiomatics, but the content itself is routine order theory.
transcription_corrections: 'Atopos (Σ)' / 'Atopat (Σ)' should read 'Atspat(Σ)' (atelier spatial, cf. 'Atspl' on p. 52). The image shows 'At spat'.
'c'est une partie fermée par Δ' should read 'fermée pour ⊴'.
'Cf. axiome Atopat 2 ci-dessous' should read 'Cf. Atspat 2 ci-dessous'.
'organisation' for Σ is uncertain; the word is hard to read and may be a term defined earlier in the notes.
'CF VIII' is likely a reference to chapter VIII (p. 9).
